title: 3.4.19 Lab: Callback Capstone
description: Write a counting helper that takes a callback, then use it with a one-line arrow to count matching values in an array. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write the counting helper
steps.instructions: Define a function called countMatching that takes an array and a test function. It should walk the array with a for loop, call the test on each element, and return how many elements passed the test.

steps.title: Prepare an array of values
steps.instructions: Create a variable holding an array of at least five numbers.

steps.title: Count with two different arrows
steps.instructions: Call the helper twice on your array, once with a one-line arrow testing one condition and once with an arrow testing a different condition. Log both counts.

requirements.title: Helper defined
requirements.description: A function is defined that accepts an array and a test function. Help: 3.4.11 (Passing a Function to a Function)
requirements.hint: The helper takes two parameters: the array first, then the function that tests each element.

requirements.title: for loop present
requirements.description: Code contains a for loop. Help: 3.3.5 (Looping Over Arrays (for / for…of))
requirements.hint: Walk the array with a for loop and look at one element per pass.

requirements.title: Callback called inside the helper
requirements.description: The test function parameter is called inside the helper. Help: 3.4.11 (Passing a Function to a Function)
requirements.hint: Inside the loop, call the test parameter with the current element and use its true/false answer to decide whether to count it.

requirements.title: At least two inline arrows passed
requirements.description: Two arrow functions appear in the file. Help: 3.4.6 (Arrow Functions)
requirements.hint: Call the helper twice and write a different one-line arrow as the test each time. Two arrows, two different conditions.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.4.11 (Passing a Function to a Function)
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: countMatching counts the elements the test accepts
requirements.description: countMatching([4, -2, 7, 0, -9, 3], n => n > 0) is 3, an array where nothing passes counts 0, and an empty array counts 0. Help: 3.4.12 (Example: Arrow Callback)
requirements.hint: Start a counter at 0. For each element, call the test with it, and add one only when the test comes back true. Return the counter after the loop.

checks.expr: typeof countMatching === 'function' && countMatching([4,-2,7,0,-9,3], n => n > 0) === 3 && countMatching([1,2,3,4,5,6], n => n % 2 === 0) === 3 && countMatching([1,2], n => false) === 0 && countMatching([], n => true) === 0
checks.fail: countMatching should count only the elements the test accepts: countMatching([4, -2, 7, 0, -9, 3], n => n > 0) is 3, and when nothing passes it is 0.
